# Habeas

> A browser extension (Chrome and Firefox, MV3, AGPL-3.0) that exports a user's OWN receipts,
> invoices and bank/card statements from services that offer no export and no API.

## How it works, and why that is the whole point

Habeas runs inside the browser session the user has already signed into. It therefore:
- never asks for, stores or transmits any password or credential;
- never fights anti-bot protection, because it inherits the user's own valid session;
- lets the user resolve MFA/OTP themselves, live, as they normally would.

This is the opposite of server-side aggregation (Plaid, Tink, TrueLayer), which holds credentials
and connects on the user's behalf. Habeas is not a payment actor and initiates no payments.

## What it is NOT

- Not a scraper service: nothing runs on a server, and no data ever reaches the developer.
- Not an aggregator: no credentials are held, and there is no account with Habeas.
- Not a background crawler: extraction is user-initiated or runs on the user's own schedule.
- Data leaves the browser only to a destination the user configures (their own Drive, Dropbox,
  WebDAV, S3, local folder, or an endpoint of their own).

## Security boundary

Every host a source touches must share one registrable domain (eTLD+1), so a session captured from
a site can only ever be replayed to that same site. Crossing domains requires an explicit allow-list
and a consent screen. Sources are declarative data, never code — remote code is impossible under MV3.

## Licensing

The extension is AGPL-3.0. The source definitions are deliberately not: every definition in the
catalogue is in the public domain under CC0-1.0, and the guide prose under CC-BY-4.0. A definition
only records how a service has arranged data that already belongs to its user — fact rather than
authorship — so it can be reused in anything at all, commercially or not, with or without credit.

## Legal posture

GDPR Art. 20 (data portability): the user's own data, in the user's own session, via user-run open
source. A service's terms may restrict automated access; this is documented and is the user's
responsibility. Source: https://github.com/habeas-dev/habeas
